title: Infosys Bets on Building AI Talent Internally as Industry Rivals Cut Jobs
excerpt: While TCS, HCLTech and Cognizant trim headcount in response to automation, Infosys is hiring 20,000 graduates, training 275,000 employees in AI and targeting a billion-dollar AI services business.
body:
• Infosys plans to hire 20,000 fresh graduates while competitors like TCS have announced layoffs of up to 12,500 employees
  • The company has trained more than 275,000 employees in AI and related technologies, including generative AI, agentic AI and prompt engineering
  • AI-related services now generate approximately $1 billion in annual revenue for Infosys, contributing about 5.5% of total revenue and growing rapidly
  • Strategic partnerships with Anthropic and Cursor, plus deployment of 500-plus AI agents across 90% of top clients, underpin the company's AI-first strategy

As artificial intelligence reshapes the global IT services landscape and forces some of India's biggest technology companies to cut jobs, Infosys is charting a distinctly different course: building AI capability from within rather than trimming its workforce.

CEO Salil Parekh has ruled out layoffs and committed to onboarding around 20,000 fresh graduates this year — matching last year's intake — even as rivals restructure. Tata Consultancy Services had planned to let go of 12,500 employees, while HCLTech, Oracle and Cognizant have all announced workforce adjustments in recent months.

"We have not done any layoffs in the last year and we don't see anything of that sort coming up. AI is expanding the scope of work, not shrinking it."

— Salil Parekh, CEO, Infosys

Reskilling at Scale

Infosys has trained more than 275,000 employees across multiple levels in AI technologies, according to the company. The training covers generative AI fundamentals, agentic AI development, AI ethics, prompt engineering and AI-assisted software development.

Engineers are being trained to build code using traditional methods and then work with foundation models and AI-driven tools. Crucially, employees are also learning to assess and validate AI-generated output — a skill Parekh described as increasingly critical.

"In training, we are encouraging the engineers to build code in the way they used to in the past, and then introduce new tools and foundation models," Parekh told Moneycontrol.

AI Revenue Crosses Billion-Dollar Mark

The reskilling effort is underpinned by tangible business results. AI-related services now contribute approximately 5.5% of Infosys's revenue and have crossed the $1 billion annual mark, according to the company. That share is expected to grow as enterprise clients accelerate deployments and move beyond proof-of-concept projects.

Infosys has deployed more than 500 AI agents across 90% of its top clients, spanning manufacturing, financial services, telecom, healthcare and retail. The company also launched over 200 agentic AI initiatives — autonomous systems that handle end-to-end workflows rather than discrete tasks.

Strategic Partnerships Anchor the Push

In February 2026, Infosys announced a strategic collaboration with Anthropic to integrate Claude AI models into its Topaz platform, enabling autonomous AI workflows for regulated sectors like telecom and financial services. A January 2026 partnership with AI-coding platform Cursor is accelerating internal engineering productivity.

The company's AI First value framework, launched earlier this year, explicitly targets a $300 billion to $400 billion incremental AI services market. Infosys signed $14.9 billion in total deals in FY26, giving it substantial revenue visibility.

Skills, Not Jobs, Are Shifting

Parekh acknowledged that entry-level roles will evolve as automation becomes embedded in workflows, but maintained that overall talent demand will hold steady. The emphasis is shifting toward deeper expertise and subject matter specialization.

"There is also more attention to deep individual knowledge and becoming a subject matter expert," he said.

The approach positions Infosys at the intersection of two priorities for the global IT industry: scaling AI capabilities while retaining the human talent needed to deliver, oversee and refine those systems. Whether that bet outperforms the cost-cutting strategies of its rivals will become clearer as AI adoption accelerates across enterprise clients in the coming quarters.
nri_angle: Infosys's hiring and reskilling strategy directly affects tens of thousands of Indian IT professionals in the US and globally who work for or compete with the company in an AI-transformed industry.
